name: Matholwch

attributes.attribute: an Irish king who married Branwen to create tighter ties with Wales
mistreated Branwen after Efnisien attacked his horses
set a trap with warriors hidden in sacks of grain
died with his troops when Bran's army returned

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Matholwch was an Irish hero. In the second branch of the Mabinogion, he was the Irish king who married Branwen, a Welsh princess. The marriage sought tighter bonds between the Irish and the Celts of Wales, but the match failed when Branwen's half-brother Efnisien attacked Matholwch's horses. Matholwch mistreated Branwen even after she bore their son Gwern. Her brothers Bran the Blessed and Manawydan brought an army to free her. Matholwch set a trap, bidding the Welsh warriors to a feast with soldiers hidden in sacks of grain. Efnisien saw the danger and killed the concealed men. In the war that followed, Bran died and all but seven Welsh heroes fell with all the Irish warriors. Branwen died of a broken heart on the journey home to Wales.
objective: Document the Irish king Matholwch of the second branch of the Mabinogion.
